threads.thread_goal: Align on current journey map, key gaps, and overall pathway design.

messages.text: Hi team, I've completed the initial mapping of our current client journey from referral through to employment. I reviewed 12 recent cases and documented the patterns. The visual map is ready in the shared drive, along with the top gaps I identified. Key findings: we have handover delays between social work and employment support (avg 5-7 days), no consistent health screening before workshop entry, and movers often don't have clear info on client needs. I've also sketched a first version of the new pathway structure with 5 main stages. Let's use this thread to align on the stages and confirm which gaps we should prioritise in the pilot. Sharing T1 summary and A1 draft now.

Thanks for the thorough work on this. The 5-stage structure makes sense to me. I'm looking at the gaps you listed—the handover delays and missing health screening are definitely things we see in practice. One question: in your sketch, where does the initial assessment sit? Is that stage 1, or does it happen before the pathway formally starts?

Good catch. In the draft, assessment is stage 1—it's the entry point where we gather social, health, and employment info all at once. That's different from now, where assessment is fragmented. The idea is that by doing it holistically upfront, we reduce the back-and-forth and give employment support and health teams the full picture from day one. Does that align with what you're thinking?

I agree with the holistic assessment approach. From a health perspective, we need to flag any physical or mental health concerns early so we can adjust support during workshops and moves. I've started drafting a short health screening checklist that could feed into stage 1. It covers mobility, mental health flags, medication, and when to escalate to clinical services. I'll have that ready by EOD tomorrow. The key is keeping it brief so it doesn't slow down intake.

That's helpful. I want to make sure the assessment template also captures employment goals and any barriers—skills gaps, confidence, work history. I'll draft the full assessment template this week, incorporating the health screening checklist once you share it. We should also include a clear consent section so clients understand what info we're collecting and how it's used. I'll reference T2 and make sure it aligns with the pathway stages.

From the moves side, I need to know early if a client has mobility issues, sensory needs, or anxiety about transitions. The assessment data will help me plan safe moves and brief the team properly. Once the assessment template is locked, I can use it to prepare move checklists. I'm also thinking about the handover between stages—we need clear notes so nothing gets lost when a client moves from assessment to workshops to workplace. Should we define those handover points now or wait until we see the full pathway?

Good question. I think we should define the handover points now as part of the pathway design. That's actually part of T6—the inter-team coordination protocol. Let me draft that in parallel with the pathway overview. The handover template will ensure each role knows what info to pass on and who's responsible next. I'll include escalation paths for any safeguarding concerns too.

So if I'm understanding the flow: client comes in, we do holistic assessment (social + health + employment), then they move into workshops, then workplace placement, with clear handovers at each step. The three gaps we should definitely prioritise are: 1) the assessment delays, 2) health screening before workshops, and 3) clear handover notes between roles. Does everyone agree those are the top three to focus on in the pilot?

Yes, those three make sense. Health screening before workshops is critical—we can't have clients in distress or unwell during group sessions. I'll make sure the checklist is simple and actionable so it doesn't add burden. And the handover notes will help me prepare for moves too, since I'll know what support each client needs.
Agreed. Clear handovers will make my job much easier and safer for clients. I'll be ready to input to the coordination protocol once it's drafted.

I agree with those three. Let me also confirm: are we saying the main stages are: 1) Assessment, 2) Workshops, 3) Workplace Placement, 4) Transition Support, 5) Follow-up? Or is there a different structure you had in mind?

Yes, that's close. My draft has: 1) Referral & Holistic Assessment, 2) Health Screening & Care Planning, 3) Employment Readiness Workshops, 4) Workplace Placement & Transition, 5) Sustained Employment & Follow-up. The health screening is its own stage because it's a gate—if there are concerns, we adjust the workshop approach or timing. Does that work for everyone?

That makes sense. Having health screening as a distinct stage means we're not rushing clients into workshops if they need support first. I think we can lock that structure. So D1 is: we agree on the 5-stage pathway structure as outlined. And D2 is: we prioritise assessment delays, health screening, and handover clarity. Should we document these decisions formally, or is this thread enough?

Let's document them in the thread outcome so we have a clear record. I'll update A1 with the final 5-stage structure and share it by EOD today. Then we can move forward with the detailed design of each stage. Next steps: I'll finalise A1 and T6 (coordination protocol), and we'll use those as the foundation for the assessment template, health checklist, and move checklist.

Perfect. I'll have the health screening checklist ready by tomorrow EOD so it can feed into the assessment template. Once I see the final pathway structure, I can also start thinking about what training the team will need.
I'll draft the assessment template by mid-week, incorporating the health checklist and the pathway stages. I'll also include the consent section and share it for review.

Once the pathway and assessment are locked, I'll start on the move checklist. I want to make sure it covers the specific needs that come out of the assessment—mobility, dignity, belongings, first-day support. I'll also think about how to brief clients before a move so they're not anxious.

Excellent. That covers the main threads for this phase. Let me summarise: we've agreed on the 5-stage pathway structure and the top 3 gaps to address. Next, we'll have the assessment template, health checklist, and coordination protocol ready by mid-week. That will unblock the workshop design, move checklist, and client info pack. I'll post updates in the weekly checkpoint thread. Thanks all for the solid input.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise assessment, health screening, and safeguarding tools.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the holistic assessment template incorporating feedback from the pathway alignment thread. It covers social background, health flags, employment history, skills, and goals. I've also included a clear consent section that explains data use and privacy. The template is in the shared drive. I've cross-referenced it with the health screening checklist that 14638 shared, so there's no duplication. I'd like feedback from employment support and health before we lock it for T2. Also, I want to make sure we're aligned on safeguarding—should we include a safeguarding risk assessment in the template, or is that separate?

Good work on the template. The health section looks solid—it captures the key flags we need. I've reviewed it against my screening checklist and there's good alignment. One thing: I'd suggest adding a field for 'medication and allergies' explicitly, since that's critical for moves and workplace support. Also, the consent section is clear, but we should make sure it's in plain language for clients with low literacy. Can you add a note about that?

Good points. I'll add the medication and allergies field and simplify the consent language. I'll also add a note that the template should be read aloud to clients if needed. On safeguarding, I'm thinking we should have a separate safeguarding flow document—that's more about what to do if we identify a concern, not just screening. That would be T9. Should I draft that, or is that someone else's task?

T9 is on my list—I'll draft the safeguarding and incident reporting flow. The assessment template should flag concerns, but the flow document will define what happens next: who to notify, timelines, escalation paths. I'll have that ready by end of week. In the meantime, let's make sure the assessment template has a clear 'safeguarding concerns' section that prompts the assessor to note any red flags.

I think the template should have a safeguarding section, yes. But I want to make sure we're not asking assessors to make judgements they're not trained for. The section should be more like 'note any concerns you observe' rather than 'diagnose safeguarding risk'. The flow document can then guide what to do with those notes. Does that make sense?

Exactly right. The template is for observation and documentation, not diagnosis. The flow will then provide clear decision trees for when to escalate. I'll make sure the flow aligns with our organisational safeguarding policy and includes timelines for reporting.

That's clear. So the assessment template will have a 'safeguarding observations' section, and the separate flow document will guide action. I'm comfortable with that approach. One more thing on the health screening: I want to make sure we have a clear referral pathway if we identify a health concern. For example, if a client discloses mental health struggles, who do they see? Is it our responsibility to refer, or do we flag it and the social worker follows up?

That's a good question for the safeguarding flow and the health screening checklist. I think the health checklist should have a 'referral triggers' section that says 'if X is noted, refer to Y service'. Then the assessment template can reference that checklist. That way, the assessor knows exactly what to do if something comes up.

Yes, that works. I'll add a 'referral triggers and pathways' section to the health screening checklist. So if a client reports depression, the checklist will say 'refer to GP or mental health service' with contact info. That way, the assessor has clear guidance.

I've been reading along. The assessment template looks good. I have a question though: once the assessment is done, who owns the next step? Is it the social worker who stays with the client, or does employment support take over? I want to make sure there's no gap between assessment and workshops.

Good question. That's where the coordination protocol (T6) comes in. The idea is that the social worker completes the assessment and then hands over to employment support with a clear handover note. The social worker stays involved for safeguarding and wellbeing checks, but employment support leads the workshop phase. The handover note will specify who's responsible for what. I'll make sure that's crystal clear in the protocol.

That makes sense. So the assessment template is the handoff point. Once it's complete, employment support gets a copy and the coordination protocol tells them what to do next. I think we're ready to lock the assessment template. Should we also lock the health screening checklist at the same time, since they're linked?

Yes, I think we should lock both together. The health checklist is part of the assessment process, so they need to be aligned. I'll finalise the checklist with the referral triggers section by EOD tomorrow, and then we can sign off on both.

I'll incorporate the medication field, plain language consent, and safeguarding observations section by EOD tomorrow. Once I see the final health checklist, I'll do a final alignment check and we can lock both. That leaves the safeguarding flow (T9) for next week, which 9716 is handling.

Yes, I'll have the safeguarding flow ready by end of week. It will include incident types, thresholds, reporting steps, timelines, and escalation paths. I'll align it with our organisational policy and share it for team review. Once that's done, we'll have D4 locked: the safeguarding and incident reporting flow is agreed across all roles.

Perfect. So to summarise: D3 is that we approve the assessment template and health screening checklist for pilot use by EOD tomorrow. D4 is that we agree on the safeguarding flow by end of week. Both are critical for the pilot to launch safely. I think we're on track.

Agreed. I'll have the health checklist finalised by EOD tomorrow. Once that's locked, I can also start thinking about the training we'll need to deliver to the team on how to use these tools. That's part of T10.

Good thinking. Once we have all the tools locked, we can plan the training. I'll coordinate that with you and 8393 to make sure everyone knows how to use the assessment, health checklist, and safeguarding flow. We'll keep it short and practical, as per the constraints.

threads.thread_goal: Shape the workshop programme and client-facing information pack.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the employment readiness workshop outline. The plan is 4 core sessions over 4 weeks: 1) Exploring Work & Confidence, 2) Job Search & Application Skills, 3) Interview Prep & Workplace Expectations, 4) Sustaining Employment & Problem-Solving. Each session is 2 hours with a mix of group discussion, practical activities, and peer support. I've designed the activities to work for mixed literacy and language levels—lots of visuals, role-play, and one-on-one check-ins. I've also drafted a simple feedback form for clients to complete after each session. The outline is in the shared drive. I'd like feedback from social work and health on whether the content and pace work for our client group.

Good structure. The 4-week timeline is realistic given our 21-day pilot window. I have a question on the content: are you building in time for clients to talk about barriers they're facing? Some of our clients have trauma, housing instability, or family pressures that affect their ability to work. I want to make sure the workshops acknowledge that, not just focus on job skills.

That's a really good point. I've included some space for that in session 1 and session 4, but I could expand it. The idea is that in session 1, we do a 'my story' activity where clients share what's brought them to the pathway and what they hope for. That opens the door to talking about barriers. And in session 4, we do problem-solving around 'what might get in the way of staying in work' and how to get support. But I could add more structured time for barrier-sharing in session 2 or 3. What do you think?

I think adding barrier-sharing time is important. From a health perspective, if clients are stressed or anxious about work, we need to acknowledge that and help them develop coping strategies. I'd suggest adding a 'wellbeing check-in' at the start of each session—just 5 minutes where people can say how they're feeling. That way, if someone's struggling, we can offer support or adjust the session. Also, I want to make sure the activities are physically accessible. Are there any standing activities, or is it all seated?

Good questions. I've designed most activities to be seated, but there are a couple of standing role-plays. I can easily adapt those to be seated or offer a choice. And the wellbeing check-in is a great idea—I'll add that to the session plan. I'll also add a note that facilitators should be trained to recognise signs of distress and know when to pause or offer a break. That ties into T10, the training plan.

I'm reading through the outline and it looks solid. One thing I want to flag: the feedback form you drafted—is it anonymous? Some clients might not want to write their name, especially if they're giving critical feedback. Also, are you planning to collect feedback verbally as well, in case clients struggle with writing?

Good catch. I'll make the form anonymous and offer both written and verbal options. I can also do a quick verbal debrief at the end of each session—just 'what worked, what didn't, what would help next time'. That way, we get feedback in real time and can adjust. I'll update the outline to include that.

I've been following this thread. The workshop outline sounds good. I'm wondering: once clients finish the 4 sessions, what happens next? Do they go straight to job search, or is there a transition period? And who's responsible for that transition—is it still employment support, or does someone else take over?

Good question. The workshops are meant to prepare clients for job search and placement. After the 4 sessions, employment support (that's me and 76106) would work with each client on their individual job search plan. We'd help them identify suitable roles, prepare applications, and practice interviews. That's not part of the workshop programme itself, but it flows from it. The coordination protocol (T6) will clarify the handover from workshops to individual job search support.

Yes, and the coordination protocol will also specify when the mover gets involved—that's when we're preparing for the actual move to a new home or workplace. So the flow is: workshops → individual job search → workplace placement → move → first-day support → follow-up. Each stage has a clear handover point.

That's helpful. So I'll be involved once a client has a confirmed job placement and needs to move. I'll need to know from the assessment and workshops what support they need—mobility, anxiety management, practical help with belongings, etc. The coordination protocol will tell me when to step in and what info I need from employment support.

Exactly. Now, let me also share that I've started drafting the client-facing information pack. It's a plain-language leaflet that explains the pathway, what to expect in workshops, client rights, and how to give feedback or raise concerns. I've kept the language simple and included some visuals. I'd like feedback from social work on whether it's accurate and accessible, and from health on whether the wellbeing and support information is clear.

I'll review the info pack for accuracy. One thing to make sure: it should explain what happens if a client has a concern or wants to withdraw. We need to be clear that they can pause or exit without penalty, and that we'll support them to find alternative options. That's part of respecting client autonomy.

Good point. And from a health perspective, the pack should also explain what support is available if someone's struggling—who to talk to, how to access mental health support, what to do if there's a crisis. I'll review the health and wellbeing section and make sure it's clear and reassuring.

I'll add those sections. So the pack will include: pathway overview, workshop details, client rights, how to give feedback, how to withdraw, and support available if struggling. I'll have a draft ready by mid-week for review.

Good. Once you have the draft, I'll review it for alignment with the pathway and safeguarding principles. Then we can lock it as D6. In the meantime, I think we're ready to lock the workshop outline as D5. The 4-session structure, accessibility adaptations, wellbeing check-ins, and feedback approach all look solid. Does everyone agree?

Yes, I'm comfortable locking the workshop outline. The accessibility and wellbeing elements are there, and the feedback loop is good. I'll make sure the training plan (T10) includes how to facilitate these sessions safely.
Agreed. The outline is solid and addresses the key concerns about accessibility and client autonomy. I'll review the info pack draft by mid-week and we can lock that as D6 shortly after.

Perfect. So D5 is locked: the workshop structure and topics are approved. D6 will follow once the info pack is reviewed. I'll have the pack draft ready by mid-week, and we can sign off by end of week. That keeps us on track for the 21-day pilot launch.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on logistics for moves, workplace transitions, and employer engagement.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the safe relocation and workplace transition checklist. It covers three phases: pre-move planning, the move itself, and first-day workplace support. The checklist includes steps to protect client dignity, manage belongings safely, and prepare clients emotionally for the transition. I've also included a section on communicating with clients before the move so they know what to expect. The draft is in the shared drive. I'd like feedback from social work and employment support on whether it covers the key concerns and whether the language is clear for the team to use.

Good work. I've reviewed the checklist and it's thorough. One thing I want to make sure: does it include a safeguarding check? For example, if we're moving a client to a new home, we should verify that the accommodation is safe and appropriate. And if there are any concerns, we should have a process to escalate. Can you add that?

Good point. I'll add a pre-move home visit checklist that covers safety, accessibility, and suitability. If there are concerns, the checklist will say 'escalate to social worker for safeguarding review'. That way, we're not making safeguarding decisions, but we're flagging issues early.

I like that approach. From a health perspective, I want to make sure the checklist also includes a health and wellbeing check before the move. For example, if a client is very anxious or unwell, we might need to delay the move or provide extra support. I can work with you to add that section.

Yes, that makes sense. I'll add a health check section that asks: 'Is the client physically and emotionally ready for the move? Are there any health concerns that need to be managed?' If there are concerns, we can coordinate with you to provide support or adjust the timing.

The checklist is looking good. I have a question on the first-day workplace support section: who's responsible for that? Is it the mover, or does employment support stay involved? I want to make sure the client isn't left alone on their first day.

Good question. I think the mover's role is to help with the physical move and settling into the new home or workplace. But for ongoing first-day support at work, that should be employment support or the employer. I can include a note in the checklist that says 'employment support to confirm first-day plan with client and employer before move day'. That way, everyone knows who's doing what.

That works. So the mover handles the logistics of the move, and employment support handles the job-readiness and first-day plan. I'll make sure that's clear in the coordination protocol. Now, on the employer side: I've been working on identifying employers for the pilot. I've compiled a list of 8 potential employers in the local area—a mix of retail, hospitality, admin, and care roles. I've had initial conversations with 5 of them, and 3 have confirmed interest. I'd like to share the employer profiles with the team and get feedback on whether they're suitable.

Good progress on the employer outreach. Before we confirm the 3, I want to make sure they understand the support our clients need and that they're willing to be flexible. Can you share the profiles so we can review them? I want to check: do they have experience with vulnerable workers, are they willing to provide reasonable adjustments, and do they have a point of contact for ongoing support?

I'll share the profiles by EOD today. I've already asked them about experience with vulnerable workers and reasonable adjustments. Two of the three have said yes, they're willing. The third is less clear, so we might need to have a follow-up conversation or look at the other 2 from the list of 5. I'll include all that detail in the profiles.

When you're reviewing the employers, can you also check whether they have a safe, accessible workplace? For example, are there accessible toilets, quiet spaces for breaks, and a supportive manager? Those things matter for clients with disabilities or anxiety.

Good point. I'll add those questions to the employer profile template. I'll ask about accessibility, break facilities, and manager support. That way, we can match clients to employers that are genuinely supportive.

I think we should also ask employers about their expectations for the pilot. For example, how long are they willing to support a client? What happens if the client struggles? Do they have a process for feedback and adjustment? That way, we're all on the same page about what success looks like.

Absolutely. I'll add those questions too. So the employer profile will cover: experience with vulnerable workers, willingness to provide adjustments, workplace accessibility, manager support, expectations for the pilot, and feedback process. I'll update the template and reach out to the 5 employers with the full set of questions. That should help us identify the best 3 to 5 for the pilot.

Good. Once you have the updated profiles, I'll review them and we can make a final decision on which employers to include. I want to make sure we're setting clients up for success, not just filling placements. Let's aim to confirm the employers by end of week so we can start matching clients.

Once the employers are confirmed, I'll want to visit each workplace to understand the layout, identify any accessibility issues, and meet the manager. That way, when I'm preparing a client for the move, I can give them accurate information about what to expect.

That's a great idea. I'll coordinate those workplace visits with the employers. We can do them once the employers are confirmed, so by end of next week. That gives us time to prepare before we start matching clients.

Perfect. So to summarise: D7 is that we approve the safe relocation and workplace transition checklist, with the additions for safeguarding, health checks, and first-day coordination. D8 is that we confirm the initial set of 3 to 5 employers for the pilot, with full profiles and workplace visits scheduled. Both should be locked by end of week. Does everyone agree?
Yes, I'm ready to lock the checklist once I've added the safeguarding and health sections. I'll have that done by EOD tomorrow.
And I'll have the updated employer profiles ready by EOD tomorrow, with the full set of questions answered. Then we can review and confirm by end of week.
Good. I'll review the employer profiles from a health and accessibility perspective and give feedback by end of week.

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, evaluation, and team rituals for the pilot.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the outcome and attendance tracking sheet for the pilot. It's a simple spreadsheet that records: client pseudonym, workshop attendance, milestones reached (e.g., completed assessment, finished workshops, secured job offer), and employment outcomes (e.g., started work, still employed at 4 weeks). All client identifiers are pseudonymised to protect privacy. I've tested it with sample data and it's clear to use. I've also drafted a pilot evaluation plan that defines key success indicators: at least 70% of clients complete the pathway, at least 50% secure employment, and positive feedback from clients and staff. I'd like feedback on whether these indicators are realistic and whether we're tracking the right things.

Good work on the tracker and evaluation plan. The success indicators look reasonable for a pilot. I have a question on the tracking sheet: are we also tracking any safeguarding incidents or concerns? We need to know if the pathway is creating any new risks or if we're identifying concerns early. Can you add a column for that?

Good point. I'll add a column for 'safeguarding concerns noted' and 'action taken'. That way, we can track whether we're identifying issues early and responding appropriately. I'll keep it high-level so we're not duplicating the detailed safeguarding flow, but we'll have visibility.

I'd also suggest tracking health-related issues or adjustments made. For example, if a client needed extra breaks due to fatigue, or if we identified a health concern that needed referral. That helps us understand whether the pathway is working for clients with health needs.

I'll add that too. So the tracker will have columns for: attendance, milestones, employment outcomes, safeguarding concerns, health adjustments, and any other support provided. That gives us a full picture of how the pathway is working.

I think the tracker is good. On the evaluation plan, I want to make sure we're also collecting qualitative feedback—not just numbers. For example, what did clients find most helpful? What was difficult? What would they change? That kind of feedback will help us improve the pathway for the next phase.

Absolutely. I've included client feedback forms in the evaluation plan—both written and verbal options. I've also included a staff debrief template so we can capture what worked and what didn't from the team's perspective. We'll do a mid-pilot review at week 2 and a final review at week 4 to see what we've learned.

Good. I want to make sure the evaluation plan also includes a process for capturing any unexpected outcomes—positive or negative. For example, if a client's family situation improves because of the support, or if we identify a new barrier we didn't anticipate. Those insights will help us refine the pathway.
I'll add a section for 'unexpected outcomes and learning' to the evaluation plan. That way, we're capturing the full picture, not just the planned metrics.

Now, on the team rituals: I've been thinking about how we stay coordinated during the pilot. We need regular check-ins to share updates, flag issues, and adjust as we go. I'd suggest: twice-weekly async standups where each role posts a quick update on what they did, what they're doing, and any blockers. Plus a weekly checkpoint thread to review progress against the backlog and adjust priorities. Does that work for everyone?

I like that cadence. Twice-weekly standups keep us in sync without being too heavy. And the weekly checkpoint gives us time to step back and look at the bigger picture. I'd also suggest a post-incident mini-review whenever something goes wrong—safeguarding issue, move problem, etc. That way, we learn quickly and adjust.

Good idea. And I'd add a rolling Q&A thread for clarifying how to use the new templates and checklists. People will have questions as they start using them, and a Q&A thread keeps the answers in one place.

Those rituals sound good. I'd also suggest an end-of-pilot retrospective thread where we capture lessons learned and ideas for improvement. That way, we're not just evaluating outcomes, we're also reflecting on the process.

Perfect. So the team rituals are: twice-weekly async standups, weekly checkpoint, post-incident mini-reviews, rolling Q&A thread, and end-of-pilot retrospective. That's D10: we confirm the cadence and format of check-ins and reviews. I'll document all of this and share it with the team so everyone knows what to expect.

I'll finalise the tracking sheet and evaluation plan by EOD tomorrow, incorporating the safeguarding, health, and unexpected outcomes sections. Then we can lock D9: we agree on the key indicators and data to track during the pilot.

I'll review the tracking sheet and evaluation plan by EOD tomorrow and give feedback. Once those are locked, I can start planning the training sessions for the team on how to use all the new tools and follow the new pathway.

Good. So by end of week, we'll have: D9 locked (tracking and evaluation), D10 locked (team rituals), and the training plan (T10) ready to schedule. That means we'll have all the operational pieces in place to launch the pilot. Let me do a final check: we've locked D1-D8 in previous threads, and we're locking D9-D10 here. That covers all the mandatory decisions. Once T10 is scheduled, we're ready to go.

That's a good summary. We've covered a lot of ground in the past week. Let me recap: pathway design (D1-D2), assessment and safeguarding tools (D3-D4), workshops and client info (D5-D6), logistics and employers (D7-D8), and tracking and rituals (D9-D10). All the pieces are coming together. I think we're on track for the 21-day pilot launch.

Agreed. Let's make sure we hit the EOD tomorrow deadlines for the tracking sheet and evaluation plan, and the end-of-week deadlines for the training plan and employer confirmation. I'll post a summary of all decisions and next steps in the weekly checkpoint thread so we have a clear record. Thanks everyone for the solid work.
